report: A young woman developed right-eye vision loss four days after a direct lightning strike to the right forehead. Although initial ocular examination was largely normal, follow-up revealed central macular thickening, delayed posterior subcapsular cataract, and OCT showing outer retinal irregularity, cystoid changes, and subfoveal ellipsoid disruption. These objective structural abnormalities are characteristic lightning sequelae and are confirmed by radiologist analysis. The temporal relationship and imaging findings strongly support lightning-induced ocular injury, while directly refuting functional/non-organic visual loss and unrelated ocular disease. Thus, the evidence converges on this diagnosis with high confidence.
answer: Lightning-induced retinopathy with delayed-onset cystoid macular abnormalities
